oversize-baggage.context: A tall golf bag standing beside a small suitcase to show the size difference. Used at airport desks and stations for items that do not fit the normal luggage belt.

lost-baggage.context: A suitcase with a bold question mark on its front. Used at airport baggage halls and rail stations to point people to the lost luggage desk.

airport-shuttle.context: A minibus in side view with a small airplane above its roof. Used for airport transfer buses and hotel shuttle stops.

kiss-and-ride.context: A car at the curb with a passenger walking away carrying a bag. Used at stations and airports for quick drop-off and pick-up zones.

pet-relief-area.context: A dog standing beside a small fire hydrant on a patch of grass. Used in airports, rest stops and apartment blocks for dog toilet areas.

rail-replacement-bus.context: A bus in side view with a small train front on its side panel. Used on timetables and station signs when buses run in place of trains.

bicycle-carriage.context: A train carriage in side view with a bicycle shown in its window. Used for bike spaces on trains and cycle-friendly service labels.

trolley-return.context: Two luggage trolleys nested in a row with a curved return arrow above. Used at airports, stations and shops to show where to leave carts.

unaccompanied-minor.context: A small child with a pouch on a lanyard around the neck and a backpack beside them. Used for airline and rail services that escort children travelling without an adult.

clear-stadium-bag.context: A see-through tote bag with short handles and small items visible inside. Used at stadiums, concerts and arenas to show the clear bag rule.

playbill.context: A slim theater program booklet with two drama masks on the cover. Used for show programs, cast lists and theater lobby signs.

apron-bus.context: A low wide airport bus in side view with several doors, in front of an airplane tail fin. Used for airside passenger buses that carry people between terminal and aircraft.

detection-dog.context: A harnessed dog standing beside a suitcase as if sniffing it. Used for security checkpoints, customs areas and border inspection signs.

night-bus.context: A bus in side view with a crescent moon and a small star above its roof. Used for late-night and overnight bus routes on maps and timetables.

amnesty-bin.context: A lidded bin with an apple being dropped in from above. Used at borders and airports where travelers can discard food before biosecurity inspection.

bus-bike-rack.context: The front of a bus with a bicycle riding on a rack below the windshield. Used on transit signs for buses that carry bikes.

car-shuttle-train.context: A flat rail wagon carrying a car in side view. Used for motorail services and tunnel shuttles that carry vehicles by train.

cable-ferry.context: A flat ferry deck on water with a mast tied to a cable strung between two river banks. Used for river crossings where the boat is guided by a cable.

firefighter-lift.context: An elevator with a closed door and a firefighter helmet above it. Used in buildings to mark the elevator reserved for fire service use.

emergency-door-release.context: A pull lever on a wall plate beside a door, with a downward arrow. Used on trains, buses and lifts to show the manual door release.

bridleway-sign.context: A rider on a horse in profile. Used on countryside signs for paths open to horse riders.

boot-cleaning-station.context: A boot pressed against upright brushes on a low tray, with spray dots beside it. Used at farms, nature reserves and trailheads to stop soil and disease spreading.

ground-nesting-birds-sign.context: A small bird sitting on a nest cup in the grass. Used at beaches, moors and heaths to ask visitors to keep dogs on leads and stay on paths.

tide-table.context: A board showing a wavy tide curve above a row of time columns, with rising and falling arrows. Used at harbors and beaches to post high and low tide times.

vinegar-station.context: A post-mounted box with a gable roof holding a squeeze bottle, with a jellyfish drawn on the box. Used on beaches where vinegar is kept for jellyfish stings.

avalanche-beacon-checkpoint.context: A post with a round sensor and signal arcs reaching a skier wearing a chest pack. Used at ski area gates where transceivers are tested before backcountry access.

ski-patrol.context: A skier wearing a backpack marked with a white cross. Used on ski maps and signs for the mountain rescue and first aid team.

ski-school.context: A large skier followed by a small skier. Used on resort maps and signs for the ski lesson meeting point.

magic-carpet-lift.context: A small skier standing on a conveyor belt that rises up a short slope under a cover line. Used on beginner areas for moving walkway lifts.

terrain-park.context: A snowboarder in the air above a curved kicker jump. Used on resort maps for freestyle areas with jumps and rails.

platter-lift.context: A skier holding a pole with a round disc seat, hanging from an overhead cable. Used for button and disc surface tow lifts on ski maps.

rope-tow.context: A skier gripping a moving rope that runs up the slope between two pulley posts. Used on small hills and nursery slopes for rope tow lifts.

pump-out-station.context: A dockside post with a hose and nozzle reaching the deck fitting of a small boat. Used at marinas for pumping out boat toilet holding tanks.

fishing-line-recycling-bin.context: A narrow upright tube bin on a post with a tangle of fishing line beside it. Used on piers and lakesides to collect discarded line safely.

fish-cleaning-station.context: A counter with a tap and sink and a fish lying flat on top. Used at boat ramps and campsites for preparing a catch.

pilgrim-route-marker.context: A square marker plate showing a scalloped shell with ribs fanning out. Used to mark long-distance walking and pilgrimage trails.

hang-gliding.context: A triangular delta wing glider with a pilot hanging beneath it. Used on signs and maps for hang gliding launch sites and flying areas.

windsurfing.context: A sailboard with a tilted triangular sail and a surfer leaning back and holding the boom. Used for beaches and lakes with windsurf rentals and launch spots.

outdoor-fitness-station.context: A park exercise frame with parallel bars and a figure doing a dip between them. Used on park maps and trail signs for outdoor workout equipment.

shoe-locker.context: A grid of small lockers with a pair of shoes in one compartment. Used at temples, spas, sports halls and schools where shoes are left at the door.

foot-shower.context: A low outdoor tap spraying water over a bare foot on a slatted platform. Used at beach and pool entrances for rinsing sand off feet.

holy-water-font.context: A shallow stone basin on a wall bracket with a fingertip dipping into it. Used at church entrances where visitors touch blessed water.

priority-queue-sign.context: Three small figures at the front of a lane: a wheelchair user, an expectant person and a person with a cane. Used at counters and gates for priority boarding and service.

fare-box.context: A pedestal fare box with a coin slot on top and a card reader panel on its face. Used on buses and trams for paying with coins or cards.

rapid-water-rise-sign.context: A warning triangle with a rising arrow above flood waves. Used near rivers, dams and low crossings to warn that water levels can climb quickly.

swift-water-sign.context: A warning triangle with a swimmer's head and arm swept along by current lines. Used at rivers and weirs to warn of strong currents.

remain-seated-sign.context: A rider seated in a ride car with a lap bar across the thighs and a downward arrow beside them. Used at amusement rides to tell guests to stay seated.

keep-arms-inside-sign.context: A rider in a ride car with one arm reaching out of the car and a line struck through it. Used at amusement rides and trains to keep limbs inside.

ride-height-requirement.context: A child standing beside a tall measuring post with a bar at head height. Used at amusement rides to check minimum rider height.

splash-zone-sign.context: A curling wave with flying droplets heading toward a seated rider. Used at water rides and shows to warn that seats may get wet.

snack-vending-machine.context: A tall vending cabinet with shelves of snack packets, a button column and a dispense slot. Used to mark snack machines in stations, offices and halls.

beach-clean-station.context: An upright board holding a litter picker and a roll of bags beside a small bin. Used at beaches to lend out gear for volunteer cleanups.

dog-tie-up-point.context: A metal ring on a wall bracket with a leash clipped to it and a small water bowl below. Used outside shops and cafes where dogs wait while owners go inside.
